purpose: Dated facts about the Delhi Police district structure around 2007 to 2010, read by Claude from the sources named here. Supports the map labels for 2002 to 2010. Not a station roster.
caveat: Station-to-district lists are now held for 2004 (Rajya Sabha) and 2014 (Lok Sabha, roster_2014.json) only. Notification numbers and the stations Outer and South-East took in 2007 and 2008 were not found.
retrieval: Read 2026-11-04. The MHA PDF is mirrored at satp.org; the mha.gov.in original returned 404 or 403 from this machine. The SHA-256 identifies the exact file read.

sources.source: MHA Annual Report 2008-09, chapter 6, Delhi Police, paragraph 6.14
sources.finding: Three police districts in 1951; six after the 1978 Delhi Police Act (East and West added); nine in 1988 (North-East, North-West, South-West added); Outer added on 5 September 2007 and South-East on 1 October 2008, making 11. Paragraph 6.15: creation of 11 new police stations and two districts sanctioned.

sources.source: PIB, Ministry of Home Affairs year-end review, 24 December 2009
sources.finding: During 2009, 22 new police stations and 9 sub-divisions of Delhi Police were notified, and sanction for 6,478 posts issued.

sources.source: Rajya Sabha unstarred question 2100, 22 December 2004, Statement (printed pp. 76 to 82)
sources.finding: 116 police stations printed under the nine police districts of 2004: East 13, New Delhi 6, North-East 11, Central 12, North 13, North-West 17, South 18, South-West 13, West 13. Station names and heading only; see roster_2004.json.

readAs: Nine police districts from 1988 until Outer on 5 September 2007, which matches NCRB printing nine districts for 2001 to 2006 and ten for 2007.
South-East began on 1 October 2008, so NCRB's 2008 table (11 districts) re-states the whole year on the new layout.
NCRB's own figures show the re-statement: North-West total IPC fell from 11,146 (2006) to 5,189 (2007) while Outer appeared with 5,690.
22 stations and 9 sub-divisions were notified in 2009, inside the period mapped with the 2014 shapes, so station moves between districts are likely.

The 2004 list puts Narela, Alipur, Bawana, Rohini, Sultan Puri, Mangol Puri and Kanjhawala under North-West, and Lajpat Nagar, Kalkaji, Okhla and Sarita Vihar under South. That is where the 2014 Outer and South-East districts later took their stations from. Vasant Vihar, R.K. Puram, Sarojini Nagar and Vasant Kunj were South-West in 2004 and are South in 2014.
